answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because summit only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, raven is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any island approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
